tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Give helper functions a new Verb-Noun name such as Read-Doc, also in script files. A built-in alias (rd, rm, del, ri, sc, mv and others) runs instead of a function with the same name, with no warning.
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
    - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, .claude/settings.local.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

# PROGRESS — master status

Claude Code reads this at the start of every session and updates it at the end. Keep it short and current; history goes in `BUILD_LOG.md`.

## Current milestone

**Session 19C (Nov 19, Opus, laptop): landing hero performance.** The 19A hero kept the main thread busy every frame (idle
37-47% desktop / 98% on a 4x-throttled phone; scroll 20 fps desktop, 9 fps phone). Measured with CDP traces, fixed the causes,
same look on desktop (frozen-frame pixel diff < 0.06%). Landing files only. Numbers, method and screenshots:
`docs/screenshots/hero-perf/` and BUILD_LOG 19C. **Next: demo video, submission.**

Decisions (S19C): phones / low-power devices (< 900 px wide, <= 4 CPU cores, or Save-Data) get a lighter hero: the light-lines
are drawn still (no drift, no glowing dots) and the stack does not spread apart on scroll; everything else (intro, breathing
stack, ring ball, card scale/dim/corners on scroll) is unchanged. All hero loops pause while the hero is off screen or fully
covered by the dark panel. Found, not fixed (out of scope): shop subdomains answer `/favicon.ico` with 404, which fails
`l-s16-themes` (6 tests) when e2e runs on full Google Chrome (`LW_CHROME`); the bundled headless browser never asks for it.

**Session 19B (Nov 19, Opus, laptop): test emails only when she asks, clearly marked TEST; everything re-checked and deployed.**
Launch / "Run checks now" / "Describe the problem" send the test order to the shop's order address; monitoring sends it to
LaunchWitness's own check mailbox (hello@), labelled as such, with no "Yes, I got it" link. Every test email starts
`TEST, not a real order:` with a grey banner and no customer links; real order emails unchanged. 19A (landing motion) was
already merged by the owner and deployed. VPS on the final `main`. **Next: demo video, submission.**

Decisions (S19B): a daily test missing from OUR mailbox is "couldn't check" (our side), never an alert to the seller; monitoring
tests go to hello@ only, even for team-run shops (one recipient), so the daily proof is always labelled "check mailbox"; the test
email drops the cancellation line, the Orders link and the pickup instruction (nothing to act on); the test order's note no longer
says "launch check"; `scripts/admin_check_shop.py` runs a manual or daily round from the CLI inside the container (audited
`admin (cli)`), because the check routes need a signed-in cookie, not `ADMIN_TOKEN`.

**Session 17 (Nov 18-19, Opus, laptop): LIVE. The first real shop is launched and proven.** Logo + favicon + app icons; one branded
email layout; demo shop https://meeras-eggless-bakes.launchwitness.com launched for real (7/7 checks, real Let's Encrypt cert, test order
found over IMAP); shared report https://launchwitness.com/r/GsZj7gOAoCydSauqdNpoaWksKHVW-HSz (chain intact); nightly backups + restore
test; the VPS deploys by `git pull` over a read-only deploy key. Four fixes found on the live run (see STATE). **Next: demo video, README,
brief PDF, submission.**

Decisions (S17): the logo's real colours (lime/cream/peach on ink) drive everything: the email button is lime with dark text (the art has
no purple), the tab icon sits on an ink tile, apple-touch/manifest on ink `#161614`; the mark is in the header only (the footer and the
sign-in page only mention the name in sentences); the free-subdomain launch proves the app's own inbox by signing in to it while the Titan
client is a stub; the app container uses public DNS (SECURITY.md, "DNS the app trusts"); the test-order wait is 120 s for launch and
"Check again", while scheduled monitoring keeps its later passes; the restore test runs into a temp folder, never into a running stack.

**Session 15 (Nov 17, Opus, cloud, unattended): where she sells, how customers pay, what the order form asks** (PR into `main`, merge after S14). Selling modes, validated delivery areas/PINs, fees, payment terms with exact UPI amounts, cancellation, food marks, break, days off, daily limit; all enforced on the server; address private. See STATE_FOR_NEXT_SESSION and SPEC §9d. CHECKS_MATRIX unchanged (no check changed; the test order only gets safe defaults).

**Session 14 (Nov 17, Opus, cloud, unattended): a theme for every kind of home business** (PR open, not merged: after the VPS smoke
test). Six themes on one engine and one safety layer; Claude picks `theme` / `accent` / `section_copy` (keys and short plain text
only), code validates and draws; rule-based fallback; look picker on Review (audited); fonts self-hosted (OFL, `docs/FONTS.md`); a
strict CSP on shop pages; honest content only (testimonials only if the seller pasted them). See STATE_FOR_NEXT_SESSION and SPEC §5a.
Decisions (S14): the hero line is the page's h1 only when the Reader provides one (else the shop name); the three old palettes
(`niche-*`) are replaced by the six themes (`niche` now only feeds the rule-based suggestion); her own About text wins over the
Reader's short paragraph; the picker's inline preview doesn't count as "looked at your preview"; the owner's switch saves at once.
**Hand-written placeholders: the `theme`/`accent`/`section_copy` values in the 12 saved Reader replies** (re-capture command in STATE).

**Session 13b (Nov 17, Opus, cloud): S13 verified on the real stack, VPS guide current, public resolvers.**
Docker prod-like stack rebuilt, `check_m1.sh --local` all PASS (now also: one `monitor_tick`, one `outbox_send`), e2e
**16/16** (2 new S13 flows: order while practice mail is down -> "retrying" -> "sent"; sign-in while the mail server is
unreachable -> "We're having trouble sending email" -> the link still arrives). After `docker compose restart app`: one
monitor job, one outbox sender, a planted `sending` row reset by the reconciler and sent. No product bug found in S13; one
stale e2e assertion fixed. `SMTP_DAILY_LIMIT=450`. `docs/NEXT_SESSION_VPS.md` updated S10.5 -> S13 with a full `.env`
checklist and a smoke test. Part 3: the daily run asks 8.8.8.8 / 1.1.1.1 / 9.9.9.9 (evidence, never an alert). Weekly
digest dropped from this week's scope (owner). Unit 1045 passed, 2 skipped.

  (120 Hz screen), frames > 50 ms 120-159 -> 7-11 of ~830 (no main-thread task > 25 ms during scroll; the rest are raster of the
  dark panel coming into view); phone x4 idle 98% -> 9-13% with the hero in view and 0.1-0.2% scrolled away, scroll 9 fps -> 33-44 fps,
  frames > 50 ms 193-197 -> 8-17, long tasks after load > 100 ms 4-6 -> 3, CLS unchanged (0.026 desktop / 0.005 phone).
  tsc, build, landing pytest 17/17; e2e 26/32 on full Chrome, the 6 failures are the shop `/favicon.ico` 404 (not landing).
- Next: demo video; optionally give shop pages a favicon.

"""Session 19D: "View shop" / "Preview" on My shops.

`live_url` is the shop's real public address, built on the server from the launch plan / subdomain and
APP_DOMAIN. It is set only for a real launched shop (also when paused, so the owner can see what customers
see); a practice or draft shop gets None (it is not on the internet: the owner uses the private preview).
Only the shop's owner gets it: another seller, a guest and a logged-out visitor never see the shop at all.
"""

from sqlmodel import Session

from app.models import Business
from app.sites.hosts import site_url
from tests.conftest import sign_in
from tests.test_m3_launch import approve, meera, plan
from tests.test_s9_phase1 import launched_shop

OWNER = "meera@example.org"


def mine(client, bid: int) -> dict:
    (row,) = [b for b in client.get("/api/businesses").json() if b["id"] == bid]
    return row


def test_draft_shop_has_no_live_url(client):
    sign_in(client, OWNER)
    biz = meera(client)
    assert biz["live_url"] is None
    assert mine(client, biz["id"])["live_url"] is None


def test_practice_launch_never_links_a_public_address(client):
    sign_in(client, OWNER)
    biz = meera(client)
    p = approve(client, plan(client, biz))
    assert p["status"] == "done"
    row = mine(client, biz["id"])
    assert row["status"] == "live" and row["practice"] is True
    assert row["live_url"] is None and row["public"] is False


def test_real_live_shop_gets_its_address_from_the_server(client, engine, settings):
    biz, _p = launched_shop(client, engine, owner_email=OWNER)
    row = mine(client, biz["id"])
    assert row["live_url"] == site_url(biz["subdomain"], settings)
    assert row["live_url"].endswith(f"://{biz['subdomain']}.{settings.app_domain}/")
    assert client.get(f"/api/businesses/{biz['id']}").json()["live_url"] == row["live_url"]


def test_paused_or_held_live_shop_keeps_its_address(client, engine, settings):
    biz, _p = launched_shop(client, engine, owner_email=OWNER)
    with Session(engine) as s:
        b = s.get(Business, biz["id"])
        b.paused, b.review = True, "held"
        s.add(b)
        s.commit()
    row = mine(client, biz["id"])
    assert row["public"] is False and row["paused"] is True
    assert row["live_url"] == site_url(biz["subdomain"], settings)


def test_only_the_owner_sees_it(client, new_client, engine):
    biz, _p = launched_shop(client, engine, owner_email=OWNER)
    other = new_client()
    sign_in(other, "imran@example.org")
    assert all(b["id"] != biz["id"] for b in other.get("/api/businesses").json())
    assert other.get(f"/api/businesses/{biz['id']}").status_code == 404
    stranger = new_client()
    assert stranger.get("/api/businesses").json() == []
    assert stranger.get(f"/api/businesses/{biz['id']}").status_code in (401, 403, 404)

## 1. SSH key, user, firewall (vps)

```bash
# (laptop) a key just for this server
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/launchwitness -C "launchwitness-vps"
cat ~/.ssh/launchwitness.pub          # paste into the VPS dashboard (SSH keys), or: ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/launchwitness.pub root@<VPS_IP>
ssh -i ~/.ssh/launchwitness root@<VPS_IP>

# (vps, as root) a normal user with your key
adduser --disabled-password [REDACTED] "" lw && usermod -aG sudo lw
mkdir -p /home/lw/.ssh && cp ~/.ssh/authorized_keys /home/lw/.ssh/ && chown -R lw:lw /home/lw/.ssh && chmod 700 /home/lw/.ssh
echo 'lw ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' > /etc/sudoers.d/lw

# key login only
sed -i -E 's/^#?PasswordAuthentication .*/PasswordAuthentication no/; s/^#?PermitRootLogin .*/PermitRootLogin no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config
grep -rl 'PasswordAuthentication yes' /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/ 2>/dev/null | xargs -r sed -i 's/PasswordAuthentication yes/PasswordAuthentication no/'
systemctl restart ssh || systemctl restart sshd

# firewall: only 22, 80, 443
ufw default deny incoming && ufw default allow outgoing
ufw allow 22/tcp && ufw allow 80/tcp && ufw allow 443/tcp && ufw allow 443/udp && ufw --force enable
```

# Production-like stack on your own computer: HTTPS through Caddy (its own local CA), real cookies
# (DEV_MODE=false), the pretend GoDaddy world (USE_FAKES=true), saved Claude answers, and every email
# caught by Mailpit (nothing leaves the machine). It never reads ../.env.
#
#   docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.local.yml up -d --build
#
# App:    https://launchwitness.localhost       (shops: https://<slug>.launchwitness.localhost)
# Mail:   http://localhost:8025                  (Mailpit inbox; sign-in links arrive here)
# Details and checks: deploy/README.md

name: launchwitness-local

services:
  app:
    env_file: !reset []
    environment:
      APP_DOMAIN: launchwitness.localhost
      APP_BASE_URL: https://launchwitness.localhost
      ADMIN_EMAIL: admin@launchwitness.localhost
      ADMIN_TOKEN: ${LOCAL_ADMIN_TOKEN:-local-stack-only-admin-token}
      DEV_MODE: "false"
      USE_FAKES: "true"
      CLAUDE_MODE: fixture
      SERVER_IP: 127.0.0.1
      MONITOR_ENABLED: "true"
      PRACTICE_STEP_SECONDS: ${PRACTICE_STEP_SECONDS:-0}
      SMTP_HOST: mailpit
      SMTP_PORT: "1025"
      SMTP_SECURITY: plain
      SMTP_USER: hello@launchwitness.localhost
      IMAP_USER: hello@launchwitness.localhost
      # The e2e suite signs up several people from one address; keep the real limits otherwise.
      SIGNIN_LINKS_PER_IP_PER_HOUR: "200"
      SIGNIN_LINKS_PER_EMAIL_PER_DAY: "100"
      VISITOR_CONTACTS_PER_DAY: "100"
      USER_DESCRIBES_PER_DAY: "50"
      VISITOR_DESCRIBES_PER_DAY: "50"
      VISITOR_LAUNCHES_PER_DAY: "50"
    depends_on:
      - mailpit

  caddy:
    environment:
      APP_DOMAIN: launchwitness.localhost
      CADDY_EXTRA_GLOBAL: local_certs

  mailpit:
    image: axllent/mailpit:v1.21.8
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8025:8025"   # web inbox + API, this computer only
    environment:
      MP_SMTP_AUTH_ACCEPT_ANY: "1"
      MP_SMTP_AUTH_ALLOW_INSECURE: "1"
    restart: unless-stopped
